title: Inquest begins into death of Ont. boy killed by father
article: An inquest has begun into the death of an eight-year-old boy stabbed three years ago in Brantford Ont., by his father, who was later shot by police and died.
The inquest in Hamilton will look at several issues, including what led to the death of Jared Osidacz, who was killed by his father Andrew during a court-ordered, unsupervised visit.
It will also examine the circumstances surrounding the shooting of Andrew Osidacz, who was holding a knife to the throat of his ex-wife when police opened fire.

But Julie Craven, Andrew Osidacz's ex-wife who is also Jared's mother, has argued that a separate coroner's inquest is needed to look into the court system and children's aid societies, and what role they played in her son's death.
Craven said she had been a victim of domestic violence for years at the hands of her ex-husband, and that the issue needs to be examined.
"The coroner has already made up his mind that domestic violence is not the main issue," she told Canwest News Service on Monday, the first day of proceedings.
Craven has said an inquest needs to probe how a violent person like her ex-husband could have been granted unsupervised access.
A law named in part for Jared was passed to make inquests mandatory when a child is killed in court-ordered visits with a parent.
But the law isn't retroactive, so Jared's inquest wasn't required to be separated from the investigation into his father's death.
Andrew Osidacz killed his son on March 18, 2006. He then showed up at Craven's home, saying he had killed their son.
He held her hostage at knifepoint for an hour before police arrived.
